domain: Finding freelance projects for Yotam to do, and recurring needs worth building once and selling to many
mission: Own the answer to 'which projects should Yotam take or build': scan allowed sources (freelance listings, complaints, manual data-entry job posts), count how often a need recurs, separate explicit from inferred, match to reusable assets, rank by ROI. Draft only.

data_questions.q: Which allowed sources were reachable and which were blocked?
Which needs recur across posters and sources, with counts and denominators?
What evidence level (1-4) does each need have, and is it explicit or inferred?
Which existing assets cover each need and how much work would reuse save?
Which opportunities are VERIFIED / NEEDS_RESEARCH / NEEDS_CORRECTION / REJECTED / POLICY_BLOCKED?
What do the numbers of this domain say (trend, anomaly, denominator, sample size), what conclusion do they support, and what would change next run because of it?

rules: Do not present an inferred need as a customer request
Draft Only: no bids, applications, tenders, messages or payments
Allowed sources only; no bypassing limits or logins
VERIFIED needs level >= 2 and >= 2 independent sources
Every claim traces to a verified line in the product file; demo data is labelled
Nothing leaves the system without Yotam's per-action approval

produce.instructions: Run demand-signals, demand-match, demand-reuse; record opportunities and audit statuses with opportunity-audit.mjs.

gates.why: opportunity ledger must be readable and consistent

benchmark.task: Scan the allowed demand sources and rank recurring needs with reuse coverage.

rubric.q: Are inferred needs never presented as customer requests?
Every ranked need has counts, sources and an evidence level?
Does it identify reusable assets and the saved effort?
